proof:
1. (Linearity.) For ω ∈ TestFormOn U n let L(ω) := ζ(ω(p)). Evaluation at p is linear on forms: (ω + η)(p) = ω(p) + η(p) and (cω)(p) = c·ω(p). Since ζ is also linear, L is a linear functional on TestFormOn U n.
2. (Pointwise convergence.) Let (ω_j) be a sequence in TestFormOn U n with TestFormOnConverges ω_j → 0. That is, there is a compact K ⊆ U with tsupport ω_j ⊆ K for all j (and tsupport 0 ⊆ K) such that, for every k ∈ ℕ, the k-th iterated derivatives D^kω_j converge uniformly on K to D^k0 = 0. We show ω_j(p) → 0 in the space of n-covectors.
 (a) If p ∈ K: uniform convergence on K for k = 0 gives D⁰ω_j(p) → D⁰0(p) (TendstoUniformlyOn.tendsto_at). The 0-th iterated derivative D⁰ω(p) is the 0-multilinear map whose value at the empty tuple is ω(p) (iteratedFDeriv_zero_apply), and evaluation at the empty tuple is continuous (continuous_eval_const). So ω_j(p) → 0(p) = 0.
 (b) If p ∉ K: for every j, p ∉ tsupport ω_j, so ω_j(p) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport) and the sequence is constantly 0.
3. (Continuity.) ζ is continuous, so L(ω_j) = ζ(ω_j(p)) → ζ(0) = 0. Hence X := ⟨L, continuity⟩ is a GeometricCurrentOn U n with X(ω) = ζ(ω(p)) for every ω. This is the argument behind SimonGMT's pointGeometricCurrentOn and TestFormOnConverges.tendsto_eval in Chapter06/GeometricPointProduct.lean; the contract does not import that file, so the argument is reproduced here.
4. (Support.) Let y ∈ spt X, so y ∈ U and y ∉ zeroRegion X. Suppose y ≠ p; we show y ∈ zeroRegion X, a contradiction. Since U is open, choose ε > 0 with B_ε(y) ⊆ U. Let r := min(ε/2, dist(y, p)/2) > 0 and W := B_r(y).
 (a) W is open and y ∈ W.
 (b) closure W ⊆ closedBall(y, r) (closure_ball_subset_closedBall), and closedBall(y, r) is compact because ℝ^P is a proper space. So closure W, a closed subset of it, is compact.
 (c) closure W ⊆ closedBall(y, r) ⊆ B_ε(y) ⊆ U, because r ≤ ε/2 < ε.
 (d) X vanishes on W: let ω ∈ TestFormOn U n with tsupport ω ⊆ W. If p ∈ tsupport ω, then p ∈ W, i.e. dist(p, y) < r ≤ dist(y, p)/2, which is impossible since dist(y, p) > 0. So p ∉ tsupport ω, hence ω(p) = 0 and X(ω) = ζ(0) = 0.
 Thus W is one of the sets whose union is zeroRegion X, so y ∈ W ⊆ zeroRegion X. This contradiction shows y = p. Therefore spt X ⊆ {p}.
key_steps: ω ↦ ζ(ω(p)) is linear on 𝒟ⁿ(U).

Test-form convergence ω_j → 0 implies ω_j(p) → 0: by uniform convergence of the 0-th derivatives on the common compact support if p lies in it, and ω_j(p) = 0 otherwise. So X is sequentially continuous.
Every y ∈ U ∖ {p} has a ball W ∌ p whose closure is compact and contained in U; every test form supported in W vanishes at p, so X vanishes on W and y ∈ zeroRegion X.
